title: Azure Functions in C#: The Isolated Worker Model
summary: A C# Azure Functions app is a .NET process that a separate host starts and calls over gRPC. Measured with Core Tools 4.16.1 and Azurite 3.38.0 on an app with HTTP, Timer and Queue triggers plus an output binding, and an MSTest suite that needs no host, on net10.0 with Azure.Functions.Sdk 1.1.0 and Worker 2.52.0. FunctionsApplication.CreateBuilder against HostBuilder, IActionResult against HttpResponseData, host.json against local.settings.json, and the plans and dates (the in-process model ended on 2026-11-10) read from the docs and marked docs only.

title: Azure Service Bus: Queues, Topics and Processors
summary: Azure Service Bus with Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus 7.21.0, measured on the local emulator. PeekLock against ReceiveAndDelete, the four settlements (complete, abandon, dead-letter, defer), DeliveryCount and the dead-letter queue, ServiceBusProcessor and its options, a lock that expires during slow work (MessageLockLost reproduced), prefetch, sessions, duplicate detection, TTL, scheduling, batches, subscription filters, ServiceBusFailureReason, registration with dependency injection, the idempotent consumer, and the retirement of the old client libraries. Entra ID, RBAC roles and Premium features are docs only.
